full_judgment:
Mr. Borhanuddin, .J: Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos.1 and 2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 14.07.1993 and 21.7.1993 respectively passed by the Subordinate Judge, (Artha Rin Adalat), Mymenshing in Other Appeal No.14 of 1991 should not be set aside and / or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Facts, necessary for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite party Nos.1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted Other Suit No.204 of 1986 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Mymensingh for declaration that the record of rights prepared in the name of the defendant relates to the suit schedule property is wrong and for a further declaration of title in the suit schedule 2 property measuring 2.14 decimals of land contending inter alia that in 30.32 decimals of land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.199, Jagmohan Namadash and Harimohan Namadash had one ana share each. Said Jagamohan Namodash died leaving 2 sons Motiram and Sutiram who inherited 7.08
acres of land in the suit schedule property. Sutiram died leaving 2 sons Jogesh and Umesh, predecessor of defendant Nos.1 and 2-4 respectively. MotiraM died leaving 2 daughters plaintiff No.1 Sumitra and Niroda, mother of defendant Nos.5 and 6. The Plaintiff No.1 inherited 1.891/2 acres of land with limited right. Defendant Nos.5 and 6 inherited same portion' of land as inherited by the plaintiff No.1. Plaintiff No.2 acquired .25 decimals of land from Plot No.1234 described in suit schedule No.2 vide a deed of exchange dated 9.3.1989 and thus the plaintiffs became owners of 2.141/2 acres of land. The S.A. record is wrong and plaintiffs came to know about the wrong recording of S.A. Khatian on 3.5.1986 after obtaining certified copy of the parcha and thereafter instituted the present suit. 

3. The petitioner as defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement contending inter alia that the suit is not maintainable and barred by limitation. Further contending that Jagomohan gifted .04 minas share to his son Sutiram vide a registered deed of gift dated 16.1.1917 and accordingly Sutiram acquired 7.56 acres of land and while in possession Sutiram died leaving sons Jogesh and Umesh. Umesh transferred 1.89 acres of larid from his share to Sudangsho, Rakhal, Probat and others. Umesh died leaving defendant Nos.2-4. Who left the country giving their share to defendant No.1 and since then defendant No.1 is in possession of that share also. S.A. record correctly prepared in the name of the father of this defendant. As Motiram used to live in his father-in-law's house, Jagomohan did not give any property to Motiram. Plaintiff No.1 has been living in the village Gujiram within Thana Trishal. It has been further contended that original deed of gift was in the custody of defendant No.1. The defendant No.1 came to Mymensingh for filing written statement and stayed at Usha Boarding aild for safety kept the original deed of gift in Custody of the Manager of Usha Boarding. In the same night, the plaintiff No.2 along with his father-in-law also stayed in the same boarding. The Manager of the boarding handed over the deed of gift to the plaintiff No.2 for which this defendant filed a Complaint Case before the Magistrate but that case was ended at the stage of investigation. The Registry office of Mymensingh was burnt on 14.4.1971 and such defendant failed to obtain certified copy of the deed of gift. Defendant No.1 is in possession of the suit land and prayed to dismiss the suit with cost. 

4. After hearing the parties, the learned Assistant Judge dismissed the suit vide his judgment and decree dated 11.11.1990 and 18.11.1990 respectively holding that from the evidence of D.Ws. it is proved that Moti Ram used to live his father-in-law's house and existence of the deed of gift dated 16.1.1917 cannot be denied and the suit land is not properly identified and demarcated. 

5. Having aggrieved the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No.14 of 1991 in the Court of District Judge, Mymensingh which was subsequently transferred in the Court of Subordinate Judge, (Artha Rin Adalat) Mymensingh for disposal. 

6. After hearing the appeal the learned Subrodinate Judge allowed the appeal vide his judgment and decree dated 14.7.1993 and 21.7.1993 respectively by setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge holding that the defendant No.1 failed to prove the deed of gift dated 16.01.1917 and story regarding relating to the deed of gift is not believable and also holding that from the photocopy of the deed of gift it can be presmed that the deed was written on an old stamp paper very recently and also held that for non payment of rent, title can not be extinguished. 

7. Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas with Mr. Shankar Chandra Das, the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners submits that the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law in holding that the plea of deed of gift is nothing but a myth without considering that the trial Court arrived at a finding that the record of right was prepared pursuant to the deed of gift and Motiram used to live his father-in-law's house and never claimed the suit property during his life time. The learned Advocate also submits that the Subordinate Judge failed to consider the legal aspect of the case that as the plaintiffs did not claim the entire property of Motiram the suit is not maintainable under Order 2 Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate next submits that the cause of action of the suit arose from the wrong record of S.A. Khatian which was finally published in the year 1963 and as such the suit is barred under Article 102 of the Limitation Act. 

8. Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate on the other hand by filing affidavit-in-opposition on behalf of the opposite party No.2 oppose the Rule and submits that the Court of appeal below after considering and assessing the evidence on record independently, rightly and Judiciously reserved the judgment and decree of the trial Court in compliance with Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate also submits that the 
plaintiffs inherits their father's property as spends according to the provision of Dayabaga School of Hindu Law of inheritance. The learned Advocate next submits that defendant No.1 failed to prove that the deed of gift dated 16.1.1917. In elaborating his submission learned Advocate submits that defendant No.1 filed a photostate copy of certified copy of the deed of gift in the Court and the Court of appeal below after assessing the said photocopy, observed that the writing of the deed of gift is very recent on an old stamp paper and arrived at a finding that the same was manufactured for the purpose of the suit. The learned Advocate submits that in paragraph No.7 of the written statement defendant No.1 admitted that the plaintiff No.1 with her family living in the suit land. The learned Advocate further submits that cause of action of the suit arose when the defendant No.1 threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs on the basis of wrong record of rights and on 3.5.1986 the plaintiffs obtained the certified copy of ROR and came to know about the wrong record of rights and the instant suit filed on 19.5.1986 within 6 years from the date of knowledge and as such the suit is very much within the time. 

9. Heard the learned Advocates, perused the revisional application, counter affidavit, judgments of both the Courts below, lower Court's record and the provisions of law. 

10. Admittedly Matiram, predecessor of the plaintiffs and Sutiram, predecessor of the contesting defendant, were the sons of Jagmohan Namodas and inherited their father in equal share in the suit schedule land. The plaintiffs are claming suit schedule land as the heirs of Motiram. On the other hand the contesting defendant oppose claim of the plaintiffs on the basis of a deed of gift dated 16.01.1917 allegedly executed by Jagomohan Das in favour of Sutiram, predecessor of defendant, depriving Motiram from his legal share because Motiram used to live in his father-in-law's House. 

11. Defendant could not produce the original deed of gift or the certified copy of the deed on the plea, as stated in the written statement, that he went to Mymensingh for filing written statement of the suit and stayed night at Usha boarding and for safety he handed over the original gift of deed to the Manager of the boarding. On the same night plaintiff No.2 with his father-in-law also stayed at the same boarding and said Manager of the boarding handed over the deed to the plaintiff No.2 and his father-in-law. It is also stated in the written statement that as the registry office was burnt in 1981, he failed to obtain certified copy of the deed. 

12. It appears that the core issue is to be determined whether Jagomohan Nomodas executed any deed of gift in favour of the predecessor of defendant whether said deed of gift was proved before the Courts below. Admittedly original deed of gift or certified copy of the deed was not produced and marked as exhibits. In this regard the relevant portion of the findings of the trial Courts is quoted herein under:
“বিবাদী তাহার লিখিত বলরা তাহার মোকদ্দমায় স্বপক্ষে ১৯১৭ সনের যে দানপত্রের দলিলের কথা উল্লেখ করেন তাহা আত্নসাতের বিস্তারিত কাহিনি লিপিবদ্ধ করিয়াছেন । এতদপ্রেক্ষিতে বিগত ৩০-৩-৮৬ ইং তারিখে সংসনসিংহের সদর রেজিষ্ট্রি মহাফেজ খানায় তল্লাসীর আবেদনও করা হয় কিন্তু মহাফেজ খানা হইতে উত্তরে বলা হয় বিগত ১৪ইং এপ্রিল ১৯১৮ সনে অগ্নিকানে্ড ১৭৯৩ হইতে রক্ষিত প্রায় ৩৫০০০ টা ভলিয়ম নষ্ট হয়। ইহাতে প্রমানিত হয় বিবাদীর বর্ণিত ১৯১৭ সনের দানপত্র দলিল উতঘাটনের ব্যাপারে তাহার সদিচ্ছার অভার ছিল না। এবং ঘটনা প্রবাহ মোকদ্দমায় দায়েরী অপরাপর কাগজপত্র এবং মৌখিক সাক্ষ্য হইওত বিবাদীর স্বপক্ষে বিগত ১৬-১-১৯১৭ ইয় তারিখের দানপত্র দলিলের অস্তিত্বের সত্যতাকে অস্বীকার করা যায় না।”

The Court of appeal below reversed the findings of the trial Court which is reproduced below: 
“১নং বিবাদী তাহার বক্তব্যর সমর্থনে বিহত ১৬/১/৯৭ ইংি তারিখের দারপত্র দলিল আইনত প্রমান করিতে পারেন নােই কিংবা উহার তথাকথিত ফটোষ্টেট কপি আইনত প্রমান করার চেষ্টাও করেন নাই। উক্ত দানপতের মূল প্রত্যায়িত কপি উষা বডিং হইতে হারানো সম্পর্কে যে অবিশ্বাস্য মনগড়া উক্তি উপস্থাপন করিয়াছন তাহা নেহাযেত হাস্যকর এবং উহার অস্তিত্ব সম্পর্কে কোন যৌক্তিকতা নাই। কানণ আদালতের নথিতে রক্ষিত দানপত্র দলিলের ফটোকপিটি আমি Judicial view তে গ্রহণ করিয়া দেখিলাম যে উহার মূল কপিটি একটি পুরনো ষ্ট্যাম্পে অতি সম্প্রতি লিথিত হইয়াছে যাহার ফলে লেখাগুলি ঝাপসাইয়া গিয়াছে। বিজ্ঞ আদালত েএতদমর্মে কোন প্রকার পর্যবেক্ষনী গ্রহণ করেন নাই। উপরোক্ত আলোচনায় ইহা নিঃসন্দেহে বলা যায় যে ১নং বিবাদী জগমোগন প্রদত্ত যে দানপত্র দলিলের অবতারনা করিয়াছেন উহা সয়মনসিংহের মহাফেজ খানা পুড়িয়া যাওয়ায় সুযোগ গ্রহণ করিয়া একটি মিখ্যা ও প্রহসনমূলক উক্তি বৈ অন্য কিছু নহে । অনুরুপ জাল দলিল প্রস্তুতের জন্য ১নং বিবাদীকে ফৌজদারী কার্যবিধি আইনের ৪৭৬ ধারার বিধান মোতাবেক শাস্তি যোগ্য অপরাধ এর নিমিত্ত সোপর্দ করা ন্যায় সংগত।’

It is apparent that the findings of the trial Court is based on assumption without any plausible reason. On the other hand the e appeal Court below after assessing the evidence on record independently arrived at a finding with cogent reasons. 

13. The trial Court also came to an erroneous findings that under the Dayabhagal School of Hindu law of inheritance the married women are not entitled to get share of their father. Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas, the learned Advocate for the opposite party also admits that this finding of the trial Court is not correct. The learned Advocate submits that correct position . of law is that after the expiry of Motiram, his two daughters Sumitra and Niroda will inherit their father as Sapindas. 

14. From Mulla's Hindu Law, it appears that Article 88 of the Principles of Hindu Law relating to Dayabhaga succession runs as follows : 

"88 Order of succession among Sapindas.- The Sapindas of the Bengal School are divided into two classes, namely, (i) Sapindas ex parte patema, and (ii) Sapindas ex parte maternal. Nos.l to 32, except the five females, namely, Nos.4, 5, 8, 14 and 20, are sapindas ex-parte paterna  5 females Nos.4, 5, 8, 14 and 20 succeed in the following order. 1-3 --  Son, grandson and great grand son, 4. widow 5. Daughter Priority amongst daughters-The unmarried daughter succeeds first; then the married daughter who has or is likely to have male issue". Thus it appears that a married daughter having a son will inherit their father. As such the findings of the trial Court that under the Dayabhaga School of Hindu Law of inheritance the married women are not entitled to get share of their father is absolutely wrong and erroneous. 

The appeal Court below rightly observed that: 

“১নং বিবাদী উপরোক্ত জগমোহন রায়ের প্রত্র মতিরামকে ত্যাজ্য পুত্র হিসাবে মন্তব্য করিয়াছেন কিন্তু িএতমর্মে কোন বিশ্বাসযোগ্য প্রমানাতি আসিতেছে না । শুধুমাত্র মতিরাম তাহার শ্বশুরালয়ে বাস করে এখন একটি অহেতুক অজুহাত উত্থাপন করিতেও দ্বিধাবোধ করেন নাই। বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত ওউক্ত মতিরামের শ্বশুরালয়ে হইতে প্রাপ্ত পৈত্রিক সম্পত্তিচ্যুত হওয়ায় একটি কারণের অবতারনা করিয়াছেন ্ হিন্দু আেইনের কোথাও এমন কোন বিধান নাই যে কোন পুরুষ ব্যক্তি শ্বশুরালয়ে বসবাস করিলে তাহার পৈত্রিক সম্পত্তি হইতে চ্যুত হন। ইহাও বিবাদীপক্ষের ১নং বাদীনির সম্পত্তি চ্যুত করার একটি অজুহাত মাত্র । হিনাদু আইনের দায়ভাগ মোতাবেক কোন ব্যক্তির পুত্র না থাকিলে পুত্রবর্তী কন্যাগন পরিত্যক্ত হন। এই ক্ষেত্রে ও মতিরামের মৃত্যুর পর পুত্রবতী ১নং বিদীনি এবং পুত্রবতী নিরাদা মতিরামের ত্যাক্ত ৩.৭৯ শতাংশ ভূমিতে প্রত্যেকে ১.৮৯ ½ শতাংশ ভূমিতে অধিকারীনি হইতে আইনত কোন বাধা নাই। যেহেতু ১নং বিবাদী তাহার কখিত দানপত্র দলিল এবং মতিরামের তাজ্যপুত্র হ্ওয়া সম্পকির্ত বিষয়ে প্রমাণ করিতে ব্যর্থ হইয়াছেন সুতরাং মতিরামের পুত্রবতী কন্যগণ ত্যক্ত সম্পত্তিতে অবশ্যই অধিকারীনি হইয়াছেন।”

15. It is apparent from the evidence on record that the alleged deed of gift dated 16.01.1917 was not marked and exhibited in the suit. Further more, the learned Subordinate Judge, as a last Court of fact recorded his suspicion relating to existence of the original deed of gift and even after assessing photocopy of the said deed of gift arrived at a finding that the photocopy is manufactured for the purpose of the suit. If the deed of gift is not proved, then question of ROR in the name of the predecessor of the defendant does not arise. On perusal of both the judgment passed by the trial Court as well as the appellate Court below it appears that the Court of appeal below after assessing the evidence on record independently reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court in compliance of Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code 
of Civil Procedure. 

16. In the case of Anowar Khatun Vs. Abdul Hye and other reported in 18 BLD (AD) 223, our apex Court held :-

"Ordinary in revision the High Court division should not interfere with the finding of fact arrived at by lower appellate Court upon re-appreciation of evidence.

" It is well settled Principle of law that the High Court in its revisional jurisdiction under Section 115 cannot interfere with the findings of fact recorded by the Court below and re-appreciate the evidence and interfere with the finding unless it is found that the findings recorded by the lower Court are perverse or there has been non-application of mind. 

17. Going through the impugned judgment, I do not find that the findings of fact recorded 
by the appellate Court below as a last Court of fact, are perverse or there has been any non-application of mind. 

18. In the result, the rule is discharged without any Order as to cost. 
19. However there will be no order as to costs. 

20. Send down the Lower Court's record at once. 

End.
